newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PCIBank hopeful Victorias talks to continue.
newsitem.headline: PCIBank hopeful Victorias talks to continue.

text.p: Philippine Commercial International Bank (PCIBank) said on Thursday it remained optimistic that the restructuring negotiations between financially-troubled Victorias Milling Co and its creditors will end with an agreement.
"I'm sure we'll find a compromise," PCIBank president Rafael Buenaventura told reporters.
PCIBank is the head of the creditors' committee negotiating settlement of the 4.423 billion peso unpaid loans of the sugar miller with 32 financial institutions.

Earlier, some banks threatened to file for Victorias' foreclosure after failing to come up with a restructuring and refinancing plan after 90 days of negotiations. Victorias and the committee have asked for another 90 days to hammer out a deal.
"We will all get hurt if we foreclose the company. It is best that we talk it over and find a compromise," Buenaventura said.
He said some banks were no longer expecting to recover all their loans after finding out that some of the collaterals were worthless.
"In the end, reality will set in. Do you want to lose 100 percent or do you want to lose 10 percent?" he added.
Earlier, PCIBank's parent JG Summit Holdings Inc said it was interested in buying a majority stake in Victorias.
